songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy set highlighted by Lazy Lightning → Supplication and soaring Morning Dew
ai_show_review.blurb: The Oakland Auditorium show delivers a high‑energy first set featuring Jack Straw, Lazy Lightning into Deal and a crisp Shakedown Street jam. Standout moments include the seamless Lazy Lightning → Supplication sequence and an emotive Morning Dew in the second set. Recording quality ranges from an excellent audience‑soundboard matrix to a crystal‑clear front‑of‑board capture.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at Oakland Auditorium on December 28, 1982 is a quintessential late‑‘82 Dead night – bright, inventive and unapologetically loose. The first set rockets off with Jack Straw and quickly settles into a tight groove that carries through Tennessee Jed, El Paso and Friend of the Devil before Jerry’s sweet‑toned lead on Lazy Lightning flows effortlessly into Supplication and lands on Deal with a grin. The band stays locked in as they spin Touch of Grey, Man Smart/Woman Smarter and Dire Wolf, building momentum for a soaring Morning Dew that caps the second set. The second half shines on Shakedown Street – Brent’s tasteful fills echo Jerry’s funky licks while Phil’s thumping bass drives the groove – and Terrapin Station emerges as a lush, space‑filled centerpiece before the drums‑and‑Space excursion leads into Throwing Stones, Not Fade Away and a heartfelt Dew. The encore’s Satisfaction and It’s All Over Now Baby Blue add humor and warmth, rounding out a night that feels both relaxed and electric. Across all available sources the matrix recording offers an excellent blend of audience ambience and board clarity, while the front‑of‑board capture delivers striking cymbal definition; together they showcase why this show remains a high point of the 1982 run.

best_recording.reason: Matrix blend is praised as crisp and well‑balanced, capturing the high‑energy performance and key moments like Lazy Lightning → Supplication and Morning Dew with excellent clarity.

key_highlights: Seamless Lazy Lightning → Supplication sequence with confident lead guitar
Funky Shakedown Street jam highlighted by Brent’s tasteful fills and Phil’s bass thumps
Emotive, soaring Morning Dew that closes the second set on a high note
Strong first‑set momentum driven by Jack Straw and tight interplay throughout

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivered confident, sweet‑toned leads on Lazy Lightning and a stellar solo on Shakedown Street; occasional vocal flubs didn’t diminish his overall inspired guitar work.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass anchored the funk groove of Shakedown Street and provided a solid, propulsive foundation throughout the set.
band_performance.Bob: Weir added humor with lyrical asides (e.g., rap in Satisfaction) and playful vocal touches on Samson & Delilah, enhancing the show’s relaxed vibe.
band_performance.Brent: Mydland mirrored Jerry’s phrasing on Shakedown Street, supplying tasteful keyboard flourishes that enriched the jam without overpowering it.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart contributed subtle textures and dynamic cymbal work that helped shape the band’s expansive second‑set flow.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann kept a steady, deep groove, especially during the drum/Space segment, driving the improvisational sections forward.
